pipeline.caption: Six steps; a person decides at the last one

flows.lead: Three flows for the administrative document lifecycle, sharing one knowledge base that grows with your institution.

f1.title: Ingest & classify
f1.desc: OCR for scans, seal and signature detection, extraction of number, date and issuing body. Automatic classification and routing into the repository.

f2.title: Search & Q&A
f2.desc: Ask in plain language across the whole repository. Every answer cites its sources and says "insufficient basis" instead of guessing.

f3.title: Impact & drafting
f3.desc: Map legal relationships, flag expired references, generate drafts on Decree 30 templates and check the format before signing.

w1.title: Hours down to minutes
w1.desc: Across ingest, search and drafting, repetitive work drops from hours of manual effort to a few minutes.

w2.title: Citations, always
w2.desc: Every answer names its source and warns as soon as a cited basis has expired.

w3.title: Institutional memory that stays
w3.desc: The repository and the legal relationship graph accumulate year after year and do not leave with staff turnover.

w4.title: Compliant with Decree 30/2020 on clerical work
w4.desc: Document format follows the national standard; a staff member always approves before issuance.

t1.title: People decide
t1.desc: A document stays pending until a staff member reviews, edits and approves it. AI never replaces that decision.

t2.title: Data on your machine
t2.desc: Original documents live on your computer. Each institution gets its own key and a fully separate workspace.

t3.title: Never used for training
t3.desc: The server only runs the AI steps and keeps no content after returning a result.

download.lead: Version {version}, released {date}. Free to download, activated with your institution key.
download.note: The current build is not code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS ask for a one-time confirmation. The installation guide walks through "Run anyway" and "Open Anyway".

q1.q: What is an activation key and where do I get one?
q1.a: Agentra issues each institution a key in the form DOCOPS-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX that opens its own workspace. Install the app, choose "No key yet (new registration)" on the activation screen and send the request from inside the app, or email us with your institution name.

q2.q: Do I need an internet connection?
q2.a: Yes, for activation and for the AI steps: OCR, classification, search and drafting. Your documents still stay on your machine.

q3.a: On your computer. The server only runs the AI steps and keeps no content after returning a result. Agentra never uses institution data to train models.

q4.q: Why does Windows or macOS warn me during installation?
q4.a: The current build has no code-signing certificate yet, so the operating system asks for a one-time confirmation. The guide shows exactly where to click "Run anyway" on Windows and "Open Anyway" on macOS.

q5.q: How do I get new versions?
q5.a: No re-download needed. In the app open Settings, the Version tab, click Check for updates, then Download and install, then Restart to install.

q6.a: Downloading and installing is free. Pricing depends on how much your institution uses; contact us for a quote.

cta.sub: Download the app, request a key right from the activation screen, and start reviewing your document repository today.

meta.title: How DocOps works: six steps, staff decide last
meta.description: A document goes through six steps: ingest, classify, search, impact, draft and staff review. AI does the heavy lifting; a person makes the final decision.

howItWorks.h1: Documents are processed by AI flows. Staff make the final decision.
howItWorks.lead: DocOps does the heavy work: reading, extraction, classification, search and drafting. Your staff, the real domain experts, always have the last word on what gets used.

s1.title: Ingest
s1.desc: OCR for scans, seal and signature detection, extraction of number, date, issuing body and summary.

s2.title: Classify
s2.desc: Determine document type, topic and validity, then route it to the right part of the repository.

s3.title: Search
s3.desc: Answers come with specific citations; guessing is blocked when the basis is missing.

s4.title: Impact
s4.desc: Trace the legal relationship graph: which document cites which, and which references have expired or are about to change.

s5.title: Draft
s5.desc: Generate drafts on Decree 30 templates, check the format and suggest replacements for expired references.

s6.title: Staff review & approve
s6.desc: A person reads, edits and approves. AI assists; it never replaces the decision.

meta.title: AI and data transparency
meta.description: Where DocOps uses AI, how people stay in control, where document data lives, and our commitments on security, ownership, Decree 30/2020 and 13/2023.

transparency.lead: DocOps is open about how it uses artificial intelligence, how people supervise it, where document data is stored and what we commit to on security, so institutions can use the software with confidence.

p1.title: Where DocOps uses AI
p1.body: DocOps uses Anthropic's Claude models for OCR, seal and signature detection, metadata extraction, classification and drafting; the model is chosen by task complexity. Deterministic checks such as date, number and validity comparisons run on your machine without AI.

p2.title: People decide
p2.body: By human-in-the-loop design, a document stays pending until a staff member reviews, edits and approves it. Only then is it stored in the repository and indexed.

p3.title: Citations and no guessing
p3.body: Every search result carries its sources: document number, article, page. When the basis is insufficient the system says "insufficient basis" instead of generating an answer.

p4.title: Data security
p4.body: Original documents live on the user's computer. The server only runs the AI steps and keeps no content after returning a result. Each institution accesses with its own key rather than personal accounts, and institutions' data is fully separated.

p5.title: Institutional knowledge belongs to you
p5.body: The document repository and the legal relationship graph are your organisation's memory; they belong to the institution and can be exported at any time.

p6.title: Legal compliance
p6.body: DocOps follows Decree 30/2020/ND-CP on clerical work (the format of administrative documents) and Decree 13/2023/ND-CP on personal data protection.

p7.title: Content ownership
p7.body: The institution keeps all rights to the documents it uploads and to the processed results. Agentra never uses institution data to train models.

p8.title: Limits of responsibility
p8.body: DocOps supports professional work; it does not replace it. AI-generated content must be checked by staff before use; the final decision and the responsibility for issuing a document rest with the institution.

p9.title: Policy updates
p9.body: This policy may change when new features or new regulations arrive. The update date is shown at the top of the page.
